title: Yuqing (Claire) Wang
text:
I am a fourth-year PhD candidate in Economics at the University of Michigan. My research interests are in behavioral, experimental, and labor economics, with a focus on gender.
My current research focuses on the marriage market and women’s careers. In my main project, I use incentivized partner-choice experiments to measure what men value in a partner’s career: her income, her work hours, and her plans after children. I also test whether women correctly predict these preferences. In other work, I study how generative AI is changing research productivity in economics.
My advisor is Christine Exley. I joined the PhD program directly after earning my BS in Economics at the University of Michigan.

title: Research
text:
Equalizing or Polarizing? Generative AI and Research Productivity in Economics
(with Tianyu Jiang)
Does generative AI narrow or widen productivity gaps in research? Using NBER working-paper records, text-based measures of AI-assisted writing, and a survey of 227 economists, we find weak evidence that AI changes average output, but large differences across researchers. Greater AI exposure narrows the output gap between researchers with and without research assistants.

title: Research

Research in progress

The Believed Ambition Penalty in the Marriage Market
Do men penalize a woman’s career when they choose a partner, and do women know what men penalize? I run incentivized partner-choice experiments in which choices are used to recommend real matches. I separate a woman’s income from her time, and her job today from her work after children.


Empire by Design: American Social Engineering and Philippine Development
(with Mika Inoue, Dean Yang, and JC Punongbayan)


Motivated Reasoning and Gender Antagonism
Third-year paper
How much do men and women misjudge the hostility of the other gender, and do people avoid information that would correct these beliefs? I study this with incentivized online surveys.
